The user then asked to keep draining without checking back in, so this session
(round 4) dropped the two-round-then-stop rule and is running the loop to
completion instead — draining, rendering, and continuing through whatever each
render refills the queue with, committing after every round, until the real
backlog (`summaries_unread`) is actually exhausted or a genuine blocker shows
up. Round 4 picked up the 20 papers + 20 concepts left pending above; all had
PDFs already attached (no `backfill` candidates), so all 20 papers were read
from the actual document. Several land close to the topic's mechanistic core:
"Step-GRPO" separates reasoning traces into semantic steps and rewards
below-average step count relative to the group's own *correct* completions,
cutting DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B's tokens 32% with no accuracy loss and,
unlike a length-penalty baseline, without the accuracy collapse on hard AIME
problems that indiscriminate token-counting causes. "ThinkBrake" proves its
log-probability-margin early-stopping rule is exactly equivalent to a
KL-regularized test-time realignment with a constant reward bonus on `</think>`,
and shows a raw-probability-gap variant of the same idea is far less robust —
a concrete lesson (log-space, not linear-space) for any confidence-based
stopping rule. "TRACE" (the ACL-2026 overthinking-structure paper, distinct
from the earlier TRACE safety benchmark read in round 1) decomposes traces into
labeled sub-thought progression graphs across 14 models and finds two
overthinking-producing patterns — Explorer (over-exploration) and Late Landing
(over-verification) — and proposes a utility-based, non-length convergence-point
definition of overthinking that several length-penalty papers in this archive
implicitly approximate without stating. "ReEfBench" grounds "logical depth" in
verifiable First-Order-Logic problems and clusters 25 models into four
behavioral prototypes (Effective Solver / Deep Wanderer / Hollow Mimic / Lazy
Guesser), finding Short CoT plus reflection can now match Long CoT's depth —
the lever is whether reflection is functionally load-bearing, not how long the
trace runs. One paper cuts the other way: the LRM-safety empirical study names
overthinking as one of five risky reasoning patterns in *safety* training data,
but finds safety-oriented reasoning specifically does *not* benefit from longer
chains the way math/code does — short or template-based safety CoT matches
long-form CoT's jailbreak robustness, a domain-specific complication of "does
more thinking help" worth remembering before generalizing any single paper's
answer. Three papers were tangential rather than off-topic outright (an
SFT-exploration training-dynamics paper, a proof-rigor failure-mode benchmark,
a data-efficient-distillation paper) — read and recorded, `relevance` field says
plainly they are not about reasoning length.

Round 5 picked up the render's refill (20 papers + 20 concepts). `backfill`
found nothing new to fetch — all 20 papers already carried a PDF from
collection, so every one was read from the actual document. This was an
unusually dense batch: nearly every paper bore directly on reasoning-length
or reasoning-quality control rather than landing tangential. "Step-GRPO",
"SIGMA", "PACE", and "Step-level Advantage Selection" each attack the same
failure differently — naive length-penalty RL either over-compresses the
early steps that anchor a derivation, ignores that harder problems need more
budget, or collapses training stability on rollouts truncated before a
correct answer completes — and SAS in particular isolates a confound worth
remembering elsewhere in this archive: shortening the training *context
window* alone, with no length reward at all, already induces compression,
so some methods' reported gains may not be doing what they claim. "ERRV"
and "Self-Reading Patterns" both locate an internal, pre-existing signal —
a hidden-state "reasoning vector," an answer-to-reasoning attention
pattern — that already distinguishes efficient from inefficient reasoning
before any intervention, framing overthinking as latent and already-encoded
rather than something that must be imposed externally. "BloomEval" gives
overthinking a definition orthogonal to token count entirely — invoking
cognitive operations above what a problem's Bloom's-taxonomy level requires
— and shows this happens even in *correct* answers, invisible to
accuracy-only metrics. "ReasonIF" and the multilingual latent-reasoning
paper both complicate the "more thinking helps" framing from a different
angle: instruction-following inside a reasoning trace degrades as problems
get harder (exactly where more reasoning is usually argued to be needed),
and the internal "already knows the answer" signal exists but is weak on
hard benchmarks and uneven across languages. "CLARO" reframes conciseness
itself as something that should emerge from well-structured reasoning
rather than being imposed by a length penalty, and documents that a naive
"be concise" instruction is measurably less stable than structure-guided
prompting. A few (Entropy in RLVR, VecCISC, Rerank Before You Reason,
Chronos, STEP) are tangential — training-dynamics or test-time-scaling
efficiency work that doesn't touch reasoning length directly — recorded
with `relevance` saying so.

Round 6 picked up the render's refill (20 papers + 20 concepts). `backfill`
found 16 fetchable PDFs this time (up from the last two rounds' zero), all
ACL 2026 Findings entries, so every paper was again read from the actual

The batch again ran unusually close to the topic's core: "ADaPT" gives one
of the clearest structural arguments in the archive for *why* naive
efficiency RL degrades reasoning — an MDP proof that only the first
(mode-selection) token actually determines efficiency, so rewarding every
token equally misassigns credit, and a directly-measured finding that
standard PPO/GRPO clipping nullifies the gradient at that one token far
more than elsewhere. "CoTJudger" is the most significant methodological
paper of the round: it converts free-form CoTs into dependency graphs and
extracts a verified "Shortest Effective Path," finding redundancy is
pervasive but takes architecturally distinct forms (DeepSeek-R1's cyclic
looping vs. Qwen3-Max's diffuse "semantic verbosity" vs. Gemini-3-Pro's
locally-over-optimized near-linear structure), and names a "reasoning
illusion" — distilled models inherit a teacher's verbosity without its
verification capability — that bears directly on DRP, STACK, Pru-CoT and
CoRD elsewhere in this archive, all of which distill from a teacher's
trace and now have a specific failure mode to check against. "AlgBench"
gives a mechanistic account of "strategic over-shift" (abandoning a
correct algorithm mid-derivation) tied to necessary low-entropy tokens
that maximum-entropy RL training implicitly penalizes — a direct caution
for the entropy-shaping methods already in this archive. "Budget Guidance"
adapts diffusion-model classifier guidance to steer reasoning length
smoothly rather than truncating it, and shows hard budget-forcing can
score *below* not-thinking-at-all under a tight budget, while its soft
alternative doesn't. A few papers (RECAP, Meta-Abilities Alignment, Inner
Monologue, CoRD) were recorded as tangential — capability-forgetting,
reasoning-capability acquisition, and faithfulness/self-awareness studies
that don't touch reasoning length — with `relevance` saying so plainly
rather than forcing a fit.
